previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a man with HCV-related cirrhosis and multifocal hepatocellular carcinoma, was admitted for altered mental status due to hepatic encephalopathy. He had experienced increasing frequency of encephalopathy episodes over recent weeks. Upon admission, he was confused but improved rapidly with lactulose. Imaging showed stable portal vein thrombosis and no new liver lesions or portosystemic shunts. His lactulose dose was increased to 30 ml three times daily to achieve 3–4 bowel movements per day, and he remained on rifaximin, warfarin, and other home medications. Labs showed stable liver and kidney function with mild hyponatremia and pancytopenia consistent with cirrhosis. He was discharged home the same day with instructions to monitor for recurrent confusion, weight gain, or infection, and to continue outpatient follow-up with hepatology and INR monitoring.

although evaluation is limited.  There is moderate ascites.

Bile ducts:  There is no intrahepatic biliary ductal dilation.  The common
hepatic duct measures 3 mm.

gallstones.

gas.

Spleen:  The spleen demonstrates normal echotexture, and remains enlarged,

recannalization, similar to CT in ___.

flow.

effusion.
